# GLM 5.2 — max

> A broad, genuinely well-layered vanilla-JS Pokedex on a competent Cloudflare Worker: 17 ESM modules with a declarative route table, a clean pub/sub store, an api layer with in-flight request dedupe, and a Worker that edge-caches PokeAPI for 24h and exposes a smart composite pokemon+species endpoint. The hard logic most entries get wrong is right here — dual-type defensive multipliers combining both types with real 0x immunities, a live 18x18 type chart, recursive branching evolution chains, correct Gen III+ stat formulas with a proper HP branch, and correct team defensive coverage. What undercuts it is a single self-inflicted contract bug plus systematic truncation. api.js:33 getPokemon() and api.js:37 getCompositePokemon() are byte-identical requests to pokemon/:id, which src/index.ts:132 answers with {pokemon, species}; I confirmed against the live deployment that /api/pokemon/25 returns exactly those two top-level keys. Every caller expecting a flat Pokemon throws on the first dereference and lands in a blanket catch that stores empty state, so all 18 type chips, all seven base-stat sorts, browse-card type badges and backgrounds, the favorites type filter, and the Pokemon-of-the-Day hero are permanently and silently wrong — which is why a smoke test reports zero console errors on a page whose filters cannot work. Layered on top: abilities.js:24 drops 214 of 373 abilities (57%, measured live), the moves dex enriches only 400 of 934, flavor entries are cut to the last 5 of ~28 with no expander, and the Forms tab is gated on pokemon.forms.length so no Mega or regional form is reachable. Nothing typed could have caught any of this: only 140 of ~4,300 lines are TypeScript and `npx tsc --noEmit` fails outright with TS2688.

## Strengths

- Correct in the parts that are hard to get right: detail.js:819-839 and team.js:248-262 multiply damage_relations across BOTH types (verified against live data for Gengar, Charizard, Magnezone, Skarmory, Sableye — all canonical, including true 0x), types.js:21 builds a live 18x18 matrix rather than hardcoding it, and detail.js:426-437 implements the real Gen III+ stat formulas with a correctly special-cased HP branch across all 25 natures (all 25 validated against PokeAPI).
- A thoughtful Worker for a live-data strategy: src/index.ts wraps every upstream call in caches.default at 24h AND emits Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 for a genuine second browser tier; compositePokemon() collapses pokemon+species into one client request under its own namespaced cache key; wrangler.jsonc run_worker_first: ['/api/*'] keeps static assets off the Worker.
- Real modular structure with no god-functions: a 12-line matchRoute over a declarative routes table, one module per view, a cohesive store.js (private-ish fields, guarded localStorage, event bus) with zero rot, and api.js:7-27 layering an in-memory Map plus a `pending` promise map for actual in-flight dedupe.
- Genuine breadth of working surfaces: six standalone dexes, a 60-tile sprite gallery including every generation's shiny variants, an interactive stat calculator, recursive evolution chains decoding 17 trigger kinds, team defensive coverage, compare, favorites, and full dual-theme tokens with an eight-keyframe animation vocabulary that is actually wired.

## Weaknesses

- One alias bug kills five surfaces permanently and silently: getPokemon() and getCompositePokemon() request the same route, which returns {pokemon, species}, so every flat-Pokemon consumer throws into a blanket catch. All 18 type chips filter an empty map, all seven stat sorts are inert (and 'total' yields NaN), browse cards never render type badges or type-coloured backgrounds, the favorites type filter always returns nothing, and the Pokemon-of-the-Day hero erases itself.
- Systematic silent truncation across the dexes: 214 of 373 abilities dropped by a `!name.includes('-')` filter (57%, measured live) so speed-boost and water-absorb do not exist in the app; 534 of 934 moves left unenriched so type/category filters and power/accuracy/PP sorts silently cover under half the corpus; items enriched to 400 of ~2180; flavor entries cut to 5 of ~28 with no expander; learnsets enriched to 100 unique moves.
- An active performance hazard: pokedex.js:308 fires enrichCards over the full 1025-entry list with no concurrency cap and no loading indicator, each fanning out to two upstream PokeAPI subrequests, and applyFilters() waits for all of them — selecting a stat sort stampedes ~2050 upstream hits and then changes nothing. There is no batch/index endpoint, which is the root cause of the typeless browse cards rather than a separate bug.
- Accessibility is near-absent: 3 aria-labels total, zero role/aria-live/tabindex, zero :focus-visible (the three :focus rules are border shifts that also set outline:none), no focus trap or restore in the modal or search overlay, no skip link, and no prefers-reduced-motion despite infinite float/shimmer/pulse animations. 20 Tab presses never place focus inside a browse card.
- Typing is effectively unenforced and rot is heavy: only 140 of ~4300 lines are TS, `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` fails with TS2688 (@cloudflare/workers-types is not a devDependency), package.json scripts are just wrangler dev/deploy/tail with no typecheck, lint or test. I scripted the import graph: 24 unused imports across 8 of 17 modules, plus 15 exported-never-imported symbols, the 20-entry type-colour map duplicated three times (data.js:1, utils.js:109, utils.js:126), the picker modal near-verbatim in compare.js and team.js each with its own hand-rolled debounce, and 135 inline style attributes over a 2125-line token stylesheet.
- Data-correctness bugs beyond the alias: evolution reads only details[0] so Leafeon loses its Leaf Stone route, compares d.gender to the string 'female' when PokeAPI returns an int (Froslass and Salazzle both label 'Male'), and double-fires on stone evolutions producing 'Use Water Stone, Use Water Stone'; the Forms tab is gated on pokemon.forms.length > 1 instead of species.varieties so no Mega/Gigantamax/regional form is reachable; the offensive panel uses Math.max/first-wins and reports Gengar as 0x vs Normal and Steel.
- Light theme is half-broken on the flagship page: styles.css:873/883/891 hardcode rgba(255,255,255,0.6-0.85) on .detail-id/.detail-genus/.detail-flavor while the header gradient goes pastel, leaving the genus and Pokedex entry at roughly 1.3:1 contrast beside near-black name text.

## Standout

The Worker's composite endpoint (src/index.ts:47) is the best single idea in the submission and the source of its worst bug in the same stroke: it collapses pokemon+species into one client round-trip and caches the merged result under its own namespaced key https://composite.local/pokemon/:id so it cannot collide with the passthrough entry — a genuinely sharp piece of edge design. But it shadows the plain /api/pokemon/:id path with a differently-shaped payload, and the client half is untyped plain JS with two identically-bodied accessors for it, so nothing in the codebase encodes or enforces the contract. That one unrecorded shape change is what silently disables the type filter, every stat sort, card type theming, the favorites filter and the home-page hero.
